manufacture: Generated fallback reconstruction of a metal crescent-style lock used at the meeting stiles of a two-panel Japanese aluminum sliding sash. One lock body carries a pivoted crescent lever and engages a separate metal receiver/keeper on the opposing sash. Fasteners are separate geometry. The previous pair of generic rubber handle blocks is disabled rather than treated as finished hardware.
dimensionsThickness: Each two-panel apartment window receives one lock assembly. The reconstruction uses a 30 mm x 82 mm x 10 mm base plate, 50 mm mounting-screw pitch, approximately 34 mm crescent radius, 22 mm pivot boss diameter and a 20 mm-wide receiver with projecting capture arms. The 50 mm screw pitch is period-supported by LIXIL/Tostem replacement parts covering Atmos II from 1996 and Thermal II/PG from 1999; all other section dimensions are conservative benchmark reconstruction assumptions rather than identification of an exact historical lock model.
materialsFinish: Primary body, pivot, crescent and receiver use the canonical aged sash-metal family (MAT_AgedAluminum) with physically metallic reflection, restrained smoothness and no emission. Small screw heads use canonical dark galvanized hardware metal (MAT_DarkGalvanizedSteel). No black rubber, painted silver edge highlight or emissive accent is permitted.
mounting: The lock base plate is mechanically fastened to one meeting stile with two visible screws on a 50 mm vertical pitch. A pivot boss carries the crescent lever. The opposing receiver is a separate U-like capture component on the other meeting stile. Components sit proud of the sash face by millimetres and may not float in front of, sink through or bridge unrelated glazing/gasket geometry.
interfacesGapsSeals: The lever-to-pivot joint, lever-to-receiver engagement zone, receiver opening, screw seating and metal-to-sash contact are explicit geometry. The latch must remain outside the optical glass surface and glazing gasket, preserve the two sash-leaf depth relationship and avoid coplanar overlap with meeting-stile faces.
orientationExposure: Vertical sheltered sash hardware on the exterior-facing window assembly. It receives coherent midsummer daylight and sky/reflection fill but is partly shielded by the meeting-stile recess. The benchmark state is dry; rain wet-film gloss is zero.
aging: Cause-based aging is limited to light UV/oxide dulling, recess grime near plate edges and localized hand/contact polish on the operating lever. Fasteners may show restrained ferrous-source aging only. No random rust cloud, chipped-damage narrative or baked highlight is allowed.
geometryVsMaterial: Base plate thickness, pivot boss, segmented crescent silhouette, receiver throat, screw heads, contact offsets and all LOD simplification are geometry. Fine extrusion direction, sub-millimetre oxidation, micro-scratches and contact polish are material/microstructure response. Illumination, Fresnel and contact shadow must come from Unity lighting rather than albedo paint.
lodPolicy: Each of the 30 windows owns an independent four-level LODGroup. LOD0 preserves base, pivot, six-segment curved crescent, U receiver and two fasteners as six renderers. LOD1 combines the manufactured silhouette into one proxy, LOD2 removes sub-pixel pivot/fastener detail while retaining lock-versus-receiver separation in the mesh, and LOD3 retains only a thin low-profile hardware silhouette before culling. All levels use purpose-built meshes and animated cross-fade at 0.006/0.003/0.0012/0.0004 screen-relative height; visible pop remains a rendered temporal critical defect.
weatheringCausality: LOD0 body/pivot/receiver use sheltered+recessed exposure with low rain, mild UV/recess grime and higher contact only on the operating lever. Fastener weathering adds the ferrous-fixture source but remains low-intensity and localized. No source-independent dirt mask is generated.
lookdevBrief: Front diffuse view: one narrow metal lock should read as discrete hardware on the meeting stile, not two rubber rectangles. 35-degree oblique: verify plate thickness, pivot projection, receiver throat and sash seating. Midsummer grazing view: metal highlight must arise from actual BRDF/reflection and remain broadened by age; no painted edge stripe. 100-percent sash crop: resolve the 50 mm screw spacing, segmented crescent silhouette, receiver gap, no glass/gasket penetration, no repeated bright phase and no z-fight. Temporal oblique motion: verify per-window LOD cross-fade without visible pop or subpixel shimmer.
sourceBasis: LIXIL's sliding-window parts taxonomy identifies separate crescent lock, lock receiver and pull-handle components rather than treating them as one rubber insert. LIXIL/Tostem part AAAZC07L is documented for Atmos II (from 1996-10), Thermal II/PG (from 1999-02) and other window families, with a 50 mm mounting-screw pitch and metal construction. LIXIL also documents older metal crescent locks with larger pitches, confirming the same mechanically fastened lock/receiver construction family. These sources support the part class and the 50 mm period-plausible pitch; they do not identify the exact benchmark building product. References reviewed 2026-09-12: https://store.lixil.co.jp/window/window-parts/sash/slidingwindow.html ; https://store.lixil.co.jp/aaazc07l.html ; https://store.lixil.co.jp/netbl00029.html .

material.uvAging: small oxidation/value/roughness drift only; lever contact may locally polish but never paint a highlight
material.angularFresnelResponse: metallic environment reflection strengthens at grazing angle according to the real BRDF; age broadens response and prevents a chrome-like mirror stripe
